name: (2019 QC4)
assessment: Traveling at a swift 47,197 km/h, this 120-meter rock poses no threat as it cruises past at a comfortable distance of 19 million kilometers. It serves as a standard celestial visitor, large enough for tracking but far enough to remain a non-issue for Earth.

name: (2016 RT17)
assessment: Clocking in at 32,154 km/h, this 117-meter asteroid remains well outside our safety perimeter at over 26 million kilometers away. Its passage offers a great opportunity for routine data collection without posing any risk to our planetary defense.

name: (2007 DK8)
assessment: This nearly kilometer-wide giant is moving at a blistering 83,613 km/h, marking it as today’s fastest and most massive cosmic visitor. Luckily, its significant miss distance of 47 million kilometers keeps this heavy-hitter as a distant curiosity rather than a kinetic threat.
